purpose: Displays structured rows for scanning and comparison (standings, orders, leaderboards) with sorting, row selection, density, sticky headers and a stacked card layout on small screens.

props.name: columns
props.type: Array<{ key: string; header: string; cell?: (row) => ReactNode; sortValue?: (row) => string | number | Date; sortable?: boolean; align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'; width?: string; isRowHeader?: boolean }>
props.description: Column definitions. Mark the name column isRowHeader.

props.name: caption
props.description: Table title for screen readers (hide visually with hideCaption).

props.name: getRowLabel
props.description: Name used in row checkbox labels ('Select Team Rockets').

props.name: mobileLayout
props.description: Small-screen behavior: horizontal scroll or label/value cards.

states.name: sorted
states.description: Active column shows arrow icon and aria-sort.

accessibility.role: table (native <table> with <caption>, <th scope>) inside a focusable, labelled scroll region

keyboard.action: Focus the scroll region (arrow keys scroll it), then sort buttons and row checkboxes in order.

screenReader: Caption names the table; table navigation commands work because real table markup is used.
Sortable headers expose aria-sort; sort changes are announced in a polite live region.
Row header cells give each row a name when navigating by cell.
accessibility.focus: Visible ring on the scroll region, sort buttons and checkboxes.
accessibility.touchTarget: Checkbox hit areas 44px on touch; sort buttons span the header text.
notes: Don't make whole rows clickable; put a Link in the row header cell instead.
Native: rendered as a list of rows with accessibilityRole="header" for the header; announce each row as a single summary label.

variants.name: compact
variants.useWhen: Dashboards and admin tools with lots of data.

variants.name: stack
variants.description: Rows become label/value cards on small screens.

do: Use isRowHeader for the column that identifies the row.
Keep column headers short; put units in the header ('Pts', 'Price (USD)').
dont: Don't put more than one interactive control per cell where avoidable.
Don't truncate important data without a way to see it in full.

example.web:
const columns: DataTableColumn<Team>[] = [
  { key: 'rank', header: '#', align: 'end', sortable: true, width: '3rem' },
  { key: 'name', header: 'Team', isRowHeader: true, sortable: true },
  { key: 'played', header: 'P', align: 'end' },
  { key: 'points', header: 'Pts', align: 'end', sortable: true },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', cell: (t) => <Tag tone={t.qualified ? 'success' : 'neutral'}>{t.qualified ? 'Qualified' : 'Active'}</Tag> },
];
<DataTable caption="Group A standings" columns={columns} rows={teams} getRowId={(t) => t.id} defaultSort={{ key: 'points', direction: 'descending' }} mobileLayout="stack" />
example.native: <DataTable caption="Group A standings" columns={columns} rows={teams} getRowId={(t) => t.id} />
